/cc @lzmhhh123 @wshwsh12
This kind of resolution seems not very gracefully and a little tricky, can you give me some advice?

@wshwsh12  As far as i know, even though i use `cast expr` to calculate return type,  it still failed to handle that SQL
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15794564/129676369-cc4891bf-43ab-430d-9dba-664b7bd68558.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15794564/129676455-1c0a6901-2cf5-4ff0-b13b-43c372065754.png)

Can you help to find this situation ?

ok, the problem may be: in `buildLogicalUnionAll` function, it should not use `expression.BuildCastFunction4Union(b.ctx, srcCol, dstType)` directly, because this function cast the value to the `dstType` including the charset and collation, but at this time, this information of `union result type` is not determined. The cast here should only consider the **`type`**, see `WrapWithCastAsString` for the difference. You may find if the `src type` is not `string`, the cast result's charset and collation will use `CharacterSetConnection` and `CollationConnection`

@xiongjiwei , if we ignore charset and collation in cast, that is if charset and collation of type a(return type of cast function) and b are empty or meaningless, how can we refer the final charset and collation from them.

> @xiongjiwei , if we ignore charset and collation in cast...

nope, we did not ignore the charset and collation in cast, what I said is we can not use the undetermined charset and collation.
let me explain it using this case: when union `date` and `int` type, the result type will be **`string`**, but at this time we do not know what charset and collation should be used so that we should cast `date` and `int` to `string` (which only cast the type but charset and collation, the charset information should be inferred automatically, see `WrapWithCastAsString` function), after the cast, we get 2 string type values with charset and collation, finally, we can infer the result charset and collation.

@xiongjiwei I see. 
> we get 2 string type values with charset and collation, finally, we can infer the result charset and collation

I got stuck by this situation. As we have two string type with binary charset and binary collation, how can we derive the result collation and charset. 

In this case, i can't distinguish the case: `select varchar_type union varchar_type` with cases in this issue. because after cast, return type, collation, charset are all the same. Originally,  for SQL like `select varchar_type union varchar_type`, we need not to do any changes about charset and collation. 

Simple resolution can be just take vachar union varchar as a special case and force the result charset and collation are right, but some execution plan will change and CI failed(see CI result).

a quick solution may looks like 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20839912/130247035-f3eec5d8-9932-4daa-96d4-d0117d02b3a0.png)
which `expression.WarpWithCast` is 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20839912/130247135-fa1415cb-3bb5-4696-b068-bd262c77767e.png)
it is same with https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/60065dfbee0a37dbad3380f6a389b970e581d64e/expression/builtin.go#L156-L173

it works well for `select d_date from all_types union select d_int from all_types;`. I did not check the other scenario or it may break any other tests.

> As we have two string type with binary charset and binary collation

we actually will not get 2 binary charset values, maybe you have something misunderstood, you can take a look at the solution above.

@xiongjiwei Indeed, This changes will change some SQL planner , you can just see my CI test. 

> which expression.WarpWithCast is

Yes, what i do is almost the same.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15794564/130316840-00cd2362-eb77-4e1f-91c1-509c2d563658.png)

**CI has been failing since this change** I am afraid this is may bring some bugs...

> This changes will change some SQL planner 

I think it is expected, I debug the test and find the charset information is not set correctly in the original code and make a redundant `cast` function appeared.
@xiongjiwei ， Hi, Can you take some time to review this PR ?
btw, could you please also test this query `select d_date from all_types union select d_int collate `binary` from all_types;`
@xiongjiwei Hi, I have resolved all the problem commented by you, can you spare some time to help review again

> btw, could you please also test this query `select d_date from all_types union select d_int collate `binary` from all_types;`

I find the query in the test, seems the test framework can not handle this scenario. Could you please run the query manually with `----column-type-info`. The result in MySQL is binary string, but tidb still utf8mb4.

@xiongjiwei , I test that SQL locally. result are 

@xiongjiwei 
Result of MySQL 5.7 is consistent with that of MySQL 8.x.  I have test the SQL you mentioned above, seems that before `WrapWithCast` CollationInfo is set wrong. see

issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

run master and 
```
CREATE TABLE `all_types` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `d_tinyint` tinyint(4) DEFAULT NULL,
  `d_smallint` smallint(6) DEFAULT NULL,
  `d_int` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `d_bigint` bigint(20) DEFAULT NULL,
  `d_float` float DEFAULT NULL,
  `d_double` double DEFAULT NULL,
  `d_decimal` decimal(10,2) DEFAULT NULL,
  `d_bit` bit(10) DEFAULT NULL,
  `d_binary` binary(10) DEFAULT NULL,
  `d_date` date DEFAULT NULL,
  `d_datetime` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `d_timestamp` timestamp NULL DEFAULT NULL,
  `d_varchar` varchar(20) NULL default NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
);

insert into all_types values(0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 1.5, 2.2, 10.23, 12, 'xy', '2021-12-12', now(), now(), '123');
```

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

```
mysql> select d_date from all_types union select d_int from all_types;
+------------+
| d_date     |
+------------+
| 2021-12-12 |
| 2          |
+------------+
2 rows in set (0.07 sec)

```
### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

```
mysql> select d_date from all_types union select d_int from all_types;
+------------------------+
| d_date                 |
+------------------------+
| 0x32                   |
| 0x323032312D31322D3132 |
+------------------------+
2 rows in set (16.10 sec)
```

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)
Master branch
